headline: Approved $12,981,570 loan application for Bartlett Bay wastewater plant and $48,500 for emergency operations center; set September 8 public hearings on new ordinance rules.
summary: Members approved a state loan application and $48,500 in ARPA reserve funds for an emergency operations center. They also approved a naming policy that bars naming public assets after current city employees. Ordinance changes on unmet social needs and electric mobility devices were set for a September 8 public hearing.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda as presented, 4-0.
Approved submitting a $12,981,570 loan application to the Revolving Loan Program, 4-0.
Approved a September 8, 2026 public hearing and ordinance changes to Chapters 14, 20, and 26, and rescinded two council policies, 4-0.
Approved a second reading and public hearing on September 8, 2026 for amendments to Chapters 22 and 36, 4-0.
Approved using up to $48,500 in ARPA Inspired Reserve Funds for an emergency operations center, 4-0.
Approved amended language for a naming policy for public assets, 4-0.
Approved excluding naming public assets after City employees who are currently employed, 4-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the Consent Agenda as presented. Mr. Smith seconded. Motion passed 4- 0.

Dr. Zigmund moved to approve the submission of the loan application for $12,981,570 to the Revolving Loan Program for construction of the Bartlett Bay Wastewater Treatment Facility Reconstruction Project and authorized the Director of Public Works to execute and manage the loan. Mr. Chalnick seconded. The motion was carried 4- 0.

Mr. Chalnick moved to hold a public hearing on 8 September 2026 and approve changes to the South Burlington City Ordinance Chapter 14, Chapter 20, and Chapter 26 and rescind City Council Policy 2022-05 and City Council Policy 2025-03. Mr. Smith seconded. Motion passed 4- 0.

Mr. Chalnick moved to hold a second reading and public hearing on 8 September 2026 on amendments to South Burlington City Ordinance Chapter 22 and Chapter 36 and to make a typographical correction as noted. Dr. Zigmund seconded. Motion passed 4- 0.

Mr. Chalnick moved to authorize the use of not more than $ 48, 500 of ARPA Inspired Reserve Funds to purchase the necessary infrastructure and equipment to fit up a modular and modern Emergency Operations Center. Dr. Zigmund seconded. Motion passed 4- 0.
Dr. Zigmund moved to approve amended language. Mr. Smith seconded. The motion passed 4- 0.
Dr. Zigmund then moved to exclude naming public assets after City employees who are currently employed. Mr. Smith seconded. Motion passed 4- 0.

MINUTES
CITY COUNCIL
18 AUGUST 2026
The South Burlington City Council held a regular meeting on Tuesday, 18 August
2026, at 6: 30 p. m., in the Auditorium, 180 Market Street, and by Zoom.
MEMBERS PRESENT: T. Barritt, Chair; L. Smith, A. Chalnick, Dr. B. Zigmund
ALSO PRESENT: J. Baker, City Manager; N. Storellicastro, Deputy City Manager;
C. McNeil, City Attorney; Chief B. Breault, Police Department; Chief S. Locke, Fire
Department; Deputy Chief C. Corbin, Fire Department; M. Machar, Finance
Director; E. Towle, Interim Public Works Director; S. Carlson, R. Doyle, A. Allen
1.  Pledge of Allegiance:
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited.
2. Instructions on exiting the building in case of emergency and review of
technology options:
Ms. Baker provided instructions on emergency exit from the building and
reviewed technology options.
3.  Additions, deletions or changes in the order of Agenda items:
No changes were made to the Agenda.
4.  Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda:
Mr. Carlson, a resident of Whatley Street, asked what it will take to get the Parks
Department to take down the trees that are blocking the view.  He said one of
those trees is dead.  Residents were told years ago that those trees would come
down.  Mr. Barritt noted that some of those trees were put there to prevent
PAGE 1
headlights from shining into people' s homes.   Mr. Carlson said the trees are 15
feet higher than the rooftops.
Ms. Allen said that in the summer of 2023, residents asked about traffic calming,
etc.  They were told the processes were being streamlined.  To date, nothing has
been done.  She felt that residents who do not have " a friend" on the City Council
are left with nowhere to turn.  She stressed that residents need better options.
5.  Councilors Announcements and Reports on Committee Assignments
and City Manager' s Report:
Council members reported on recent meetings and events they had attended.
Ms. Baker:  Thanked voters for having approved the bond issue.
A Green Community Festival will take place in front of City Hall on 19
September.
Milling and paving will start on Dorset Street this week.
Steel piles for the bike- ped bridge will start being installed this week
or next.
The Library Staff will be marching with Burlington Pride.
Registration for the Fly By 5K event at the Airport is full.
Congratulations to Fire Chief Steve Locke who has been sworn in as
the 150th President of the International Association of Fire Chief.  Chief Locke will
wear his South Burlington Fire Department patch for the duration of his terms.
6.  Consent Agenda:
a.  Consider and Sign Disbursements
b.  Designate SP& F Attorneys, P.C. to conduct the City' s tax sale
process
c.  Authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with
William & Lee Incorporated regarding the easement acquisition
for Parcel 12 of the Williston Road Streetscape Project
d.  Approve the request to apply for Northern Border Regional
Commission Catalyst Program grant funding to support Phase II
CITY COUNCIL18 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 2
of the Walk Bike Bridge and authorize the submittal of a letter of
support and commitment to match grant funds
e.  Receive Amendment# 1 to the Grant Agreement with SB3C to
reflect FY27 budgeted funds and updated priorities
f.   Approve Minutes from 3 June 2026, 17 June 2026, 29 June 2026, 7
July 2026, and 20 July 2026 City Council Meetings
Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the Consent Agenda as presented.  Mr. Smith
seconded.  Motion passed 4-0.
7.  Approval of State Revolving Loan Program Application for Bartlett
Bay Wastewater Treatment Facility Refurbishment Project -
Construction Phase ( Step Ill) Loan:
Ms. Baker said this increases the amount based on the positive bond vote.  It also
becomes part of the low- interest loan for the full amount.
Dr. Zigmund moved to approve the submission of the loan application for
12, 981, 570 to the Revolving Loan Program for construction of the Bartlett Bay
Wastewater Treatment Facility Reconstruction Project and authorized the Director
of Public Works to execute and manage the loan.  Mr. Chalnick seconded.  The
motion was carried 4- 0.
8.  Approve the construction contract for the Bartlett Bay Wastewater
Treatment Facility:
Ms. Towle said the contractor has been holding the bid price until the bond vote
was passed.
Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the construction contract for planned Bartlett Bay
Wastewater Treatment Plant improvements following the successful bond
authorization vote on 11 August 2026, and authorize the Director of Public Works
to execute and manage the contract.
9.  Receive and hold a first reading of an update to South Burlington
City Ordinance Chapter 14 ( Environment), Chapter 20 ( Miscellaneous
Offenses), Chapter 32 ( Streets, Sidewalks, and other Public Spaces),
and Chapter 36 ( Traffic and Vehicles), and rescind City Council Policy
2022- 05 and 2025- 03.  Possibly set a public hearing for September 8,
2026 at 7: 00 p. m.  These changes address behaviors related to unmet
CITY COUNCIL18 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 3
social needs that impact both an individual' s quality of life and the
quality of life of the greater community:
Ms. Baker said this is a follow- up to what the Council heard on 1 June.
Chief Breault said the changes can be defined as addressing critical, non- criminal
issues related to not receiving adequate social, medical, or community support.
They address how to get people to the right services and eliminate unnecessary
law enforcement contact.  The approach is to do what is best to help each person
get connected to appropriate services.
Chief Breault then outlined elements of the program:
a.  To encourage people to accept services
b.  To identify gaps in services
c.  To help remove obstacles
d.  To provide the community with a single point of contact
e.  To identify needs on an individual basis
Specific actions will include:
a.  Finalizing an agreement for contracted services
b.  Enacting a Civil Ordinance ( tonight)
c.   Providing training to Officers and City staff
d.  Developing and maintaining data
Dr. Zigmund said this is a very compassionate and rational approach.  She asked
how it works in practice.
Specific Ordinance recommendations were then addressed as follows:
1.  Prohibit the unsafe disposal of drug paraphernalia that would harm a
child who might get in contact with it ( Chapter 14, Article II, Section 14-
85)
2.  Prohibit consumption of an alcoholic beverage in a public place.
Prohibit having in one' s possession an open alcoholic or intoxicating
beverage container ( Chapter 20, Article IV, Section 20- 27)
3.  Prohibits the erection of a shelter or tent within any public right- of-way,
sidewalk, or public space within the City without a permit issued by the
City ( Chapter 32, Article IV, Section 32- 96)
CITY COUNCIL18 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 4
4.  Prohibits any pedestrian from stopping or standing on any portion of the
roadway including traffic islands ( Chapter 36, Article III, Section 36-234)
Mr. McNeil recommended language allowing for violations to be diverted to either
a community justice center or another appropriate diversion program.
Dr. Zigmund asked if these changes might have the result of having folks move to
another community.  Chief Breault said that is not the intent.  The intent is to
connect people to services.
Mr. Smith asked what happens with individuals who continue to be resistant to
being connected to services.  Chief Breault said they will issue an appearance to
Civil Court and will bring all the evidence of opportunities that have been offered
to the individual.  The Judge will be asked to assist the City.  The Chief cited the
need to hold people accountable.
Mr. Chalnick asked what the " accountability" is.  Mr. McNeil said a civil ticket or
fine.  He added that in some places in the country these offenses become criminal
after a period of time.  South Burlington does not have a criminal ordinance.  That
is left to the State.
Mr. Chalnick questioned whether a person can be prevented from standing on a
median.  Chief Breault showed a photo of a crash where a vehicle went onto the
median and would have injured someone standing there.  He stressed this is a
safety issue.  Mr. McNeil presented language to this effect.
Mr. McNeil noted that some activities are allowed on medians if the City Manager
has deemed them safe.  Chief Breault said the Police would put out cones and
advance warnings for such events.
With regard to the erecting of structures, Chief Breault said people would be given
reasonable notice and would be given help in finding shelter and services.  He
stressed it is not the intent to criminalize homelessness.  Immediate needs will be
addressed.
Mr. Smith asked if this approach has been shared with other jurisdictions, as a
regional approach would be helpful.  Ms. Baker said the Community Outreach
team is regional.  This approach has been shared with them.  Chief Breault said
they are dealing with people in crisis, and what South Burlington is attempting to
do is to get to people between crises.
CITY COUNCIL18 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 5
Mr. Chalnick moved to hold a public hearing on 8 September 2026 and approve
changes to the South Burlington City Ordinance Chapter 14, Chapter 20, and
Chapter 26 and rescind City Council Policy 2022- 05 and City Council Policy 2025-
03.  Mr. Smith seconded.  Motion passed 4-0.
10. Receive and hold a final reading of updates to South Burlington City
Ordinance Chapter 22 ( Parks and Recreation) and Chapter 36 ( Traffic
and Vehicles).  Possibly set a public hearing for September 8, 2026,
at 7: 00 p. m.  These changes address electric mobility devices as
recommended by the Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee:
Chief Breault noted this issue is at the forefront of the Bike/ Ped Committee.  The
recommendations come from them and are endorsed by the Police Department.
Mr. McNeil said some e- bikes would be allowed, others would not.   Section 36-
401 would eliminate skateboards from the prohibition.  Section 36- 403 reads that
pedestrians have the right of way on trails.
Mr. Smith noted he has seen pedestrians walking 4 abreast or wearing
headphones.  He stressed these are transportation paths.  He suggested a code of
conduct for pedestrians as well as for vehicles.  Mr. McNeil said as they go
forward, they can look at changes to the ordinance.  Chief Breault noted that
section 406 says that all users should stay to the right except when passing.
Dr. Zigmund asked about enforcement.  She is getting more and more calls from
members of the public.  Chief Breault said they have taken action against illegal
operation of a vehicle by a minor and have educated parents as to why this is
illegal.  Officers are on the paths on foot and on bicycles and can deal with
enforcement when appropriate.
Mr. Chalnick asked if a bike could be confiscated.  Chief Breault said they can with
a minor, and the parents would be required to pick up the child, the bike, and a
ticket.  He stressed that the intent is to change the behaviors.
Mr. Smith cited an incident with minors on the Burlington bike path this past
weekend and was grateful this issue is being addressed now.  Dr. Zigmund said
her concern with children operating motorized bikes is that there could be an
accident that results in injury or death.
CITY COUNCIL18 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 6
Mr. Chalnick moved to hold a second reading and public hearing on 8 September
2026 on amendments to South Burlington City Ordinance Chapter 22 and Chapter
36 and to make a typographical correction as noted.  Dr. Zigmund seconded.
Motion passed 4- 0.
11. Receive an update on the Emergency Operations Center
modernization and possibly approve a request for the use of up to
48, 500 from ARPA Inspired Reserve Funds for the purpose:
Deputy Fire Chief Corbin said he and Chief Breault are requesting using the funds
to establish a modern modular emergency center.  They have thought the Police
Station was the best location with City Hall as a second choice.  The Miller Room
would not lose its present functions.  The funds would be used for equipment,
storage, etc., and would be a one- time allocation.
Ms. Machar has said this will leave $ 1,772, 000 remaining in ARPA Inspired
Reserve Funds.
Dr. Zigmund asked if specific equipment has been priced out.  Deputy Chief
Corbin said " to the nearest dollar."
Mr. Chalnick moved to authorize the use of not more than $ 48, 500 of ARPA
Inspired Reserve Funds to purchase the necessary infrastructure and equipment
to fit up a modular and modern Emergency Operations Center.  Dr. Zigmund
seconded.  Motion passed 4- 0.
12. Discuss and possible approve a Naming Policy for Public Assets:
Ms. Baker reviewed the history.  She noted the Council had not made a decision
regarding employees and noted there are several situations that could be
considered:
a.  Do nothing
b.  Allow for activities outside of the person' s employment
c.  Consider a former employee who has done exceptional things
Mr. Smith liked the " do nothing" option as there could be a situation that can' t be
imagined at this time.
CITY COUNCIL18 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 7
Both Mr. Chalnick and Dr. Zigmund would like some statement regarding
employees.  Mr. Barritt didn' t want to name something for a current City
employee, nothing more.
Dr. Zigmund said there are other ways to recognize an employee.
Dr. Zigmund moved to approve amended language.  Mr. Smith seconded.  The
motion passed 4- 0.
Dr. Zigmund then moved to exclude naming public assets after City employees
who are currently employed.  Mr. Smith seconded.  Motion passed 4- 0.
13. Review the significant agenda topics for the Council' s 8 September
2026 Council meeting:
a.  Interview Development Review Board candidates
b.  Receive an update on the Building and Thermal Implementation
Plan and consider what actions to take in parallel
c.  Hear a presentation from Champlain Valley Office of Economic
Opportunity
d.  Discuss and possibly approve the FY28 Budget schedule
e.  Discuss and possibly approve a process to develop a 2027
Legislative agenda
14. Other Business:
No other business was presented.
As there was no further business to come before the Council Mr. Smith moved to
adjourn.  Mr. Chalnick seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.  The meeting was
adjourned at 8:35 p. m.
